misconceptions.description: Assuming more media automatically improves learning
misconceptions.trigger: learner treats extra audio, visuals, and effects as automatically beneficial
misconceptions.feedback: Multimedia helps only when it supports cognition. Unnecessary media can create extraneous processing and overload the learner.

misconceptions.description: Assuming identical narration and full on-screen text always reinforce one another
misconceptions.trigger: learner recommends duplicating narrated content word-for-word on the screen
misconceptions.feedback: Redundant presentation can overload the visual channel. Designers should think carefully about how text, narration, and graphics interact rather than simply duplicating content.

misconceptions.description: Treating Mayer's principles as fixed commands rather than context-sensitive design heuristics
misconceptions.trigger: learner applies a principle without considering audience, task, or media conditions
misconceptions.feedback: Mayer's principles are evidence-based heuristics, not magic rules. Designers still need to interpret them in context.
